question: Does actual Cordis AgentLoop/JSONL Session preserve raw log and reconstructed requests across separate process lifecycles, reject active writer conflicts, and distinguish not-started from unknown tool outcomes in cold repair?
fixtures: Own Vitest entry drives actual source plugins and native locking. Fixed model adapter; real fixture tool appends own effect file. Interrupted records constructed through actual persistence seam, not claimed as measured arbitrary process crash. Each phase runs a separate Node process.
oracle: Normal actual loop fixed tool call and answer: two adapter requests, exactly one target effect, authoritative disk events contain original tool output/result/answer; live second resume rejects writer ownership.

Fresh-process resume: same session ID, prior exact event prefix/derived messages survives with zero adapter requests before followup; external pre-step plugin requests series and next actual call logs corresponding request header; no prior effect rerun.

Cold repair fixtures separately: assistant tool request without tool/call gets TOOL_NOT_STARTED; durable tool/call without result gets TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and sourceEventSeqs cites original call; no model or tool invoked by resume, original prefix remains exact.
Torn uncommitted physical final fragment is discarded while complete prefix remains; invalid complete line rejects instead of accepting/truncating corruption.
Raw target JSONL and independent Python observer determine observations; no success flag substitutes evidence.
stop_conditions: Normal, resume, seed, repair phases each<=60s; fixed normal2calls/resume1call; stop on unexpected invalid setup with preservedbatch. No fullmonorepo/fullprovider tests.
limits: Crash fixtures test actual cold repair over explicitly constructed durable prefixes, not arbitrary tool-process crash timing.
Unknown-warning text does not mechanically enforce query/pause before future unsafe retries.
Selected plugins do not prove all released migration paths/power-loss durability; native flock build must be real.
No accepted execution-id/payload/version binding inferred from SessionId.
